sections.html:
Orchard Park is a town with a village inside it. The town covers 38.52 square miles about 14 miles southeast of downtown Buffalo, so find out whether your lot is in the village or the surrounding town before you call any office. The area split from Hamburg in 1850, was called Ellicott and then East Hamburgh, and took its present name on March 1, 1934.

Hamlets within the town limits include Armor, Duells Corner, Ellicott, Loveland and Webster Corners. Highmark Stadium is in the hamlet of Windom on the western edge, and Chestnut Ridge Park, the largest park in Erie County, is at the southern end. US 219 runs along the west side, US 20 across the north, and NY 277 and NY 240 meet near US 20.

Buyers ask about schools early. The Orchard Park Central School District runs four K-5 buildings named Eggert, Ellicott, South Davis and Windom, plus one middle school and one high school. Naming the right elementary school in your listing saves a round of questions.

The town had 29,804 residents in mid-2025, living in 12,829 households. Owners occupy 74.5 percent of homes, a typical owned home is valued at $360,700, and renters pay a median of $1,304 a month. Owners with a mortgage pay a median of $2,323 a month, and those without one pay $910.

People tend to stay put: 91.6 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Fewer listings can mean that a well-prepared house draws attention, so presentation and clean paperwork count.

sections.h2: Which Orchard Park offices handle permits, assessments and recording?
sections.html:
Four offices cover nearly every step of a sale.

  • Assessor's Office: keeps your assessment, takes informal review requests and receives grievance paperwork. Phone 716-662-6420.
  • Building Inspector and Code Enforcement: permits, inspections and zoning verification letters, from the Municipal Center on South Buffalo Street in the village. The counter closes for lunch from 1 PM to 2 PM on weekdays.
  • Town Board: meets on the first and third Wednesdays of each month in the Municipal Building courtroom.
  • Erie County Clerk: records the deed and collects the transfer tax.

Rezoning around the stadium and zoning map amendments have been under review in town. If your parcel is near the stadium or on a corridor being studied, request a zoning verification letter from the building office before you settle on a price.

Complaints are heard only in the spring, around Grievance Day, which falls on the fourth Tuesday of May. The Assessor's Office runs on this calendar and reports a 1990 revaluation, a uniform level of assessment of 28.5 percent and 12,412 parcels.

With a 28.5 percent level, the assessed figure on your notice sits far below market value, so do not read it as a price. Hearing requests are due ahead of Grievance Day, hearings run from 4 PM to 8 PM in the Town Hall basement meeting room, and the town does not take requests by email or upload. Bring Form RP-524 and backup documents, with copies for each of the five review board members. Call the assessor for the current year's schedule and read the assessment review page first.

A house inside the village may carry a second assessment, because villages that assess property take their own RP-524 complaints. Ask the assessor whether yours does.

sections.h2: What does Erie County charge a seller at the deed stage?
sections.html:
An Orchard Park seller owes a combined state and county transfer tax of $4.50 on every $500 slice of the price, and a partial slice counts as a whole one. The state takes $2.00 of that and Erie County takes $2.50. The clerk collects it when the deed is handed in. Owners 62 or older who have lived in a one or two family house for a year or more can sign an affidavit, free at the clerk's office, that drops the rate to $2.00 per $500.

Recording is billed separately. On the clerk's residential deed schedule the statutory fee is $45, each written side of a page adds $5, Form TP-584 costs $10 and the RP-5217 transfer report costs $125, so a three-page deed totals $195. The additional 1 percent mansion tax starts at $1 million and the buyer pays it.

sections.h2: Paperwork that can slow a closing
sections.html:
The biggest item is the state's seller questionnaire. Under Real Property Law 462, the owner of a house with up to four units signs it and gives it to the buyer before the buyer signs the contract. As-is wording in the contract stays legal. Several questions line up with local houses:

  • Do certificates of occupancy exist for the building?
  • Does water come from the municipal system or a well, and does waste go to a public sewer or a septic tank?
  • Has the lot had flooding, drainage trouble or water in the structure?
  • Which school district serves the address?

Work begun before a permit is issued costs a double fee. The permit list includes decks, fences, sheds, pools, roofing, furnace and air conditioning replacements, generators and added plumbing fixtures, and the town has asked for plumbing permits on all plumbing work since January 2020. Owners must also clear snow and ice from sidewalks beside their land. Close out or document any gap before an inspector or a buyer finds it.

sections.h2: When does a cash purchase suit an Orchard Park owner?
sections.html:
A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal or approval, so what remains is title work, state forms and recording. Owners consider it when they want to skip showings and repairs, as with an inherited house or a move with a fixed date.

Whichever route you choose, gather the tax bill, permit records for past work and the Erie County deed details first. Get any offer in writing, settle who covers each closing charge, and have a New York attorney read the contract. The disclosure form, the transfer tax and any lien payoff stay on the seller's side of the table.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller cover Orchard Park's transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller. The combined rate is $4.50 per $500 of price, split into $2.00 for the state and $2.50 for Erie County. Owners 62 or older who have lived in a one or two family house for a year can claim the reduced $2.00 rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Orchard Park house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes. State law lets both sides agree to an as-is sale. You still hand over the signed seller questionnaire before the buyer signs, so answer from what you know and attach any inspection reports you hold.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Orchard Park?
faqs.a: The fourth Tuesday of May. Call the Assessor's Office for the exact date, the appointment deadline and how many copies of the complaint form to bring.

faqs.q: What should I do about unpermitted work on my Orchard Park house?
faqs.a: Speak with the building office before you list. Work started without a permit costs a double fee, and the state questionnaire asks about certificates of occupancy. Closing out the permit, or disclosing the gap, is cheaper than reopening a contract later.

faqs.q: Which office records an Orchard Park deed?
faqs.a: The Erie County Clerk. On the clerk's schedule a three-page residential deed costs $195 to record, and the transfer tax is paid in the same visit. Title companies and attorneys normally file for you.
